reference.title: Dumbbell Close Grip Curl
reference.listing: Video; data sheet: body part Upper Arms, equipment Dumbbell, exercise type Strength
reference.note: Reference used only to identify the movement. No GymVisual media is stored here; this rig, model and animation are original.

breathing.pattern: Exhale as you curl up, inhale as you lower.
breathing.cadence: About 1.2 s up, short squeeze, about 2.4 s down

prescription.progression: Load is user-chosen: pick a dumbbell you can curl for the target reps with 1-3 reps in reserve (RIR 1-3, clinical opinion); add reps, then weight.

cues.text: Stand tall, dumbbells in front of the thighs, palms forward, the inner ends of the dumbbells almost touching.
Breathe out and curl both dumbbells together, elbows close to the body, hands staying close.
Squeeze at the top with the dumbbells in front of the chest; wrists straight.
Breathe in and lower slowly, 2-3 s, to straight arms.
Arms straight, dumbbells close together, repeat.

mistakes.mistake: Hands drifting apart as the weight rises
mistakes.fix: Keep the inner plates a finger width apart all the way.

mistakes.mistake: Swinging the hips to start the weight
mistakes.fix: Stand tall, brace, and use a lighter dumbbell.

mistakes.mistake: Elbows flaring out to the sides
mistakes.fix: Keep the elbows in front of the hips and close to the body.

mistakes.mistake: Dropping the weight on the way down

kinematics.norm: Full range: mean elbow range was about 117-123 degrees across barbell, EZ-bar and alternating dumbbell curls (Marcolin 2018)

kinematics.measure: Forearm rotation (wrist pron channel, 0 = palm up/forward, 90 = thumb up)
kinematics.norm: The supinated grip gave the highest biceps activity in the lifting phase; neutral grips shift work toward the brachioradialis (Coratella 2023)

kinematics.measure: Upper arm from the trunk line (sagittal)
kinematics.norm: Elbows stay near the sides; a small forward drift at the top is normal, a big swing shifts work to the front deltoid (clinical opinion)
Controlled, about 1 s up and 2-3 s down (clinical opinion); biceps activity was lower while lowering than lifting at the same load (Oliveira 2009)
Narrower than the standard curl: inner plates nearly touching (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual #415212, Dumbbell Close Grip Curl, video (movement reference)
Coratella et al. 2023, biceps brachii and brachioradialis excitation in biceps curl exercise: different handgrips, different synergy (Sports 11(3):64; PMC10054060)
Marcolin et al. 2018, differences in electromyographic activity of biceps brachii and brachioradialis while performing three variants of curl (PeerJ 6:e5165; PMC6047503)
Oliveira, Matta, Alves, Garcia and Vieira 2009, effect of the shoulder position on the biceps brachii EMG in different dumbbell curls (J Sports Sci Med 8(1):24-29; PMC3737788)

cautions: Elbow or shoulder pain: lighten the dumbbell and shorten the range; stop if pain is sharp (clinical opinion).
Keep the wrists straight (in line with the forearm); a bent-back wrist under load strains the forearm (clinical opinion).
Pick the dumbbells up and set them down with a straight back and bent knees.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
Wrist or elbow discomfort with the hands close: widen the grip slightly (clinical opinion).
modify: Back strain: do it seated or against a wall.

muscleNotes.biceps_r: Main elbow flexor and supinator; the palms stay up. Grip changes the biceps/brachioradialis share (Coratella 2023); the hands-close position is commonly said to bias the outer (long) head, which no study we found has measured (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.biceps_l: Main elbow flexor and supinator; the palms stay up. Grip changes the biceps/brachioradialis share (Coratella 2023); the hands-close position is commonly said to bias the outer (long) head, which no study we found has measured (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.forearm_extensors_r: Brachioradialis (mapped to the forearm extensor region) assists elbow flexion, most with the forearm near neutral.
muscleNotes.forearm_extensors_l: Brachioradialis (mapped to the forearm extensor region) assists elbow flexion, most with the forearm near neutral.
muscleNotes.forearm_flexors_r: Wrist and finger flexors hold the handle and keep the wrist straight.
muscleNotes.forearm_flexors_l: Wrist and finger flexors hold the handle and keep the wrist straight.
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_r: Steadies the shoulder so the upper arm stays put; it rises if the elbow drifts forward.
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_l: Steadies the shoulder so the upper arm stays put; it rises if the elbow drifts forward.
muscleNotes.core: Keeps the trunk still so the hips do not swing the weight up.
